stem: How many formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded sequencing samples and how many sequencing batches made up the clinical data set analyzed in this study?
choices: 12,103 samples from 1454 batches
1454 samples from 12,103 batches
12,103 samples from 415 batches
3105 samples from 1454 batches
answer: 12,103 samples from 1454 batches
label: Methods · cohort

stem: By what combination of median fold change (mFC) and normalized MAD (mad/mFC) did the study define a gene as batch-affected within a sequencing batch?
choices: mad/mFC >0.25 with mFC <0.75 or >1.25
mad/mFC <0.25 with mFC <0.75 or >1.25
mad/mFC <0.25 with mFC between 0.75 and 1.25
mad/mFC <0.75 with mFC <0.25 or >1.25
answer: mad/mFC <0.25 with mFC <0.75 or >1.25
label: Methods · batch-effect criterion

stem: In the two-dimensional kernel density estimation used to set the batch-effect cutoffs, what range of mFC values did the 95th highest density region span?
label: Methods · density boundary

stem: Substituting a hemizygous deletion and a single-copy gain against a diploid baseline at a representative tumor purity of 50% into the estimated copy number equation yielded which pair of fold-change values?
label: Methods · threshold validation

stem: Why was the median absolute deviation of fold changes divided by the median before being used as a batch-effect metric?
choices: MAD values tend to scale with the median
MAD values are undefined when the median falls below 1
MAD values are more sensitive to outliers than the median is
MAD values differ systematically between DNA and RNA library types
answer: MAD values tend to scale with the median
label: Methods · normalized MAD

stem: What did adding MAD as a second metric let the framework identify, given that homozygous deletions and amplifications genuinely occur in specific genes?
choices: Genes with high intrabatch variability, whose shift is confined to a few samples
Genes with low intrabatch variability, whose shift is shared across the batch's samples
Genes whose fold change drifted between sequencing runs rather than within a batch
Genes whose coverage tracked GC content rather than probe efficiency
answer: Genes with low intrabatch variability, whose shift is shared across the batch's samples
label: Methods · why MAD

stem: What moving-average PR score threshold served as the batch-level alert criterion, and what deviation from the maximum pass rate does it represent?
choices: 95.0, a deviation of at least 5% from a 100% pass rate
99.0, a deviation of at least 1% from the cohort mean pass rate
99.0, a deviation of at least 1% from a 100% pass rate
90.0, a deviation of at least 10% from a 100% pass rate
answer: 99.0, a deviation of at least 1% from a 100% pass rate
label: Methods · PR alert

stem: When target genes were sorted by median fold change within a single real-world sequencing batch, what did the ranking reveal?
choices: Fold changes clustered tightly around 1.0, with no gene near the detection thresholds
A different set of genes exceeded the thresholds in each batch
Genes exceeding the thresholds occurred only in samples with tumor purity below 50%
Some genes exceeded the threshold used for mutation detection
answer: Some genes exceeded the threshold used for mutation detection
label: Results · within-batch ranking

stem: Beyond outliers within a single batch, what pattern in the affected target genes pointed to external factors driving the fold-change variation?
choices: They were recurrently affected during specific periods
They were affected only during the first year of the four-year period
They were affected only in samples sequenced on the NovaSeq instrument
They were affected in proportion to the number of samples in each batch
answer: They were recurrently affected during specific periods
label: Results · recurrence over time

stem: Which genes consistently showed abnormally high or low median fold change in more than 10% of sequencing batches, regardless of the batch itself?
choices: CHEK1, PALB2, PMS2, and MSH2
HIST1H3A, NOTCH1, MCL1, and ZBTB7A
ARID1A, MCL1, PDPK1, and FGF19
BRCA1, BRCA2, KEAP1, and STK11
answer: HIST1H3A, NOTCH1, MCL1, and ZBTB7A
label: Results · recurrently affected genes

stem: How were the deviations of genes with recurrently elevated or suppressed median fold change distributed over the sequencing timeline?
choices: Confined to one contiguous period of instrument malfunction
Concentrated in the batches sequenced during the first year
Across the entire timeline, not confined to a particular time frame
Concentrated in batches containing fewer than 16 samples
answer: Across the entire timeline, not confined to a particular time frame
label: Results · temporal spread

stem: What criterion did the change point detection analysis apply to separate persistently deviating genes from sporadically affected ones?
choices: Aberrant fold change across at least five consecutive sequencing batches
Aberrant fold change in at least 10% of all sequencing batches
Aberrant fold change in at least three samples within a single batch
Aberrant fold change across at least three consecutive sequencing batches
answer: Aberrant fold change across at least three consecutive sequencing batches
label: Results · change point criterion

stem: How many genes did change point detection identify as carrying recurrent median fold-change shifts across the cohort?
label: Results · gene count

stem: Of the 52 genes with recurrent median fold-change shifts, how did the significantly affected genes split between gain-direction and loss-direction shifts?
choices: 37 gain-direction and 14 loss-direction
14 gain-direction and 37 loss-direction
26 gain-direction and 26 loss-direction
14 gain-direction and 11 loss-direction
answer: 14 gain-direction and 37 loss-direction
label: Results · shift direction

stem: How did normalized MAD (mad/mFC) values compare between affected and unaffected periods for the 52 recurrently shifted genes?
choices: They rose significantly in 44 of 52 genes, inflating intrabatch variability
They fell significantly in 44 of 52 genes, suppressing intrabatch variability
They did not differ significantly in 44 of 52 genes, leaving intrabatch variability stable
They differed significantly in 51 of 52 genes, mirroring the median fold change
answer: They did not differ significantly in 44 of 52 genes, leaving intrabatch variability stable
label: Results · intrabatch variability

stem: What did a systematic median fold-change deviation combined with preserved intrabatch consistency indicate about the origin of the shift?
choices: A recurrent somatic copy number alteration shared by tumors in the batch
A tumor-purity effect concentrated in the batch's low-purity samples
A sample-level artifact introduced during formalin fixation
Technical bias acting at the batch level, shared by every sample in the batch
answer: Technical bias acting at the batch level, shared by every sample in the batch
label: Results · bias versus biology

stem: What did analysis of median fold change across all sequencing batches show for mismatch repair deficiency (MMRD) pathway genes?
choices: They stayed within the predefined stable range across all sequencing runs
They showed batch-associated copy number loss during specific periods
They showed batch-associated copy number gain during specific periods
They left the stable range in roughly 10% of batches
answer: They stayed within the predefined stable range across all sequencing runs
label: Results · MMRD genes

stem: Which homologous recombination genes showed significant batch-associated copy number loss during specific sequencing periods?
choices: PMS2 and MSH2
CHEK1 and PALB2
BRCA1 and BRCA2
MCL1 and ZBTB7A
answer: CHEK1 and PALB2
label: Results · HRD genes

stem: In the representative 16-sample batch, how many samples showed ARID1A fold change below the 0.75 deletion threshold, and how many below the gene-specific cutoff of 0.656?
choices: 9 of 16 below 0.75, and 11 of 16 below 0.656
13 of 16 below 0.75, and 3 of 16 below 0.656
11 of 16 below 0.75, and 9 of 16 below 0.656
16 of 16 below 0.75, and 11 of 16 below 0.656
answer: 11 of 16 below 0.75, and 9 of 16 below 0.656
label: Results · ARID1A example

stem: In that same 16-sample batch, how many samples showed MCL1 fold change above the 1.25 copy gain threshold, and how many above the gene-specific cutoff of 1.624?
choices: 11 of 16 above 1.25, and 9 of 16 above 1.624
3 of 16 above 1.25, and 13 of 16 above 1.624
13 of 16 above 1.25, and 9 of 16 above 1.624
13 of 16 above 1.25, and 3 of 16 above 1.624
answer: 13 of 16 above 1.25, and 3 of 16 above 1.624
label: Results · MCL1 example

stem: Under what condition did the study report that a batch-associated deviation became more pronounced and riskier to interpret?
choices: When the gene, its cytoband, chromosomal arm, or whole chromosome showed consistent copy number change
When the batch contained fewer than 16 samples
When the affected gene lay outside the panel's secondary analysis targets
When the gene's fold change fell between the general and gene-specific cutoffs
answer: When the gene, its cytoband, chromosomal arm, or whole chromosome showed consistent copy number change
label: Results · regional concordance

stem: How does the framework present batch-level median fold change to the interpreter for genes that exceed both thresholds?
choices: As an automatic correction factor applied to the observed fold changes before reporting
As a reference value beside the observed fold changes, with no automated correction applied
As a filter that withholds genes flagged as batch-affected from the report
As a per-sample weighting applied to coverage before the CNV call is made
answer: As a reference value beside the observed fold changes, with no automated correction applied
label: Results · reference, not correction

stem: How is the PR score used for rapid batch-level screening defined?
choices: The proportion of samples exceeding both thresholds, over the batch's total samples
The proportion of batches exceeding both thresholds, over the cohort's total batches
The proportion of genes exceeding both thresholds, over the total target genes
The ratio of median fold change to normalized MAD across the batch's target genes
answer: The proportion of genes exceeding both thresholds, over the total target genes
label: Results · PR score

stem: In what two forms did the study conclude that tumor-only batch effects manifest?
choices: Sudden deviations confined to a specific time point, and gradual drift within each individual batch
Recurrent persistent biases spanning multiple batches, and sample-level artifacts of formalin fixation
Gene-specific capture loss, and instrument-specific decline in base quality
Sudden deviations confined to a specific time point, and recurrent persistent biases spanning multiple batches
answer: Sudden deviations confined to a specific time point, and recurrent persistent biases spanning multiple batches
label: Discussion · two manifestations

stem: What limitation did the authors state about the data underlying their framework?
choices: It came from a single institution and a single sequencing panel
It came from a single institution but four different sequencing panels
It came from three institutions sharing one standardized protocol
It mixed tumor-only and paired-normal workflows
answer: It came from a single institution and a single sequencing panel
label: Discussion · generalizability

stem: Which tumor-biology situation did the authors warn could shift a batch-level median and introduce systematic misclassification?
choices: Several tumors in one batch having tumor purity above 80%
Several tumors in one batch sharing a recurrent alteration such as 1p/19q codeletion
A single tumor in the batch carrying a homozygous deletion
A batch processed with a different reagent lot than the panel of normals
answer: Several tumors in one batch sharing a recurrent alteration such as 1p/19q codeletion
label: Discussion · median confounding

stem: Which validation step did the authors state they did not perform on the flagged copy number deviations?
choices: Statistical comparison of affected against unaffected periods
Recalculation of fold changes against a rebuilt panel of normals
Orthogonal confirmation by methods such as FISH, SNP array, or immunohistochemistry
Independent review of the flagged genes by a second pathologist
answer: Orthogonal confirmation by methods such as FISH, SNP array, or immunohistochemistry
label: Discussion · no orthogonal validation

stem: Lacking orthogonal testing, on what basis did the authors separate true copy number events from batch-associated artifacts?
choices: Agreement between the TSO500 Local App and the DRAGEN TSO500 pipeline
Concordance of the flagged genes with the panel of normals for that batch
Restriction of the flagged genes to samples with tumor purity above 60%
Absence of clinically suspected alterations, plus several genes affected in one batch
answer: Absence of clinically suspected alterations, plus several genes affected in one batch
label: Discussion · inferred distinction

stem: Why could the authors not attribute the observed batch effects to specific experimental factors?
choices: Prospective lot-level records for reagents and probes were absent
The sequencing instrument was not recorded in the sample metadata
The affected batches were too few to support a regression analysis
Tumor purity had not been assessed for the affected batches
answer: Prospective lot-level records for reagents and probes were absent
label: Discussion · unattributed cause

stem: What did the authors recommend accompany CNV results submitted to public repositories such as cBioPortal?
choices: Raw coverage files for every target interval on the panel
Batch identifiers and batch-level median fold-change metrics
The panel of normals used for each submitted sample
Tumor purity estimates and fixation times for each sample
answer: Batch identifiers and batch-level median fold-change metrics
label: Discussion · reporting recommendation

stem: How should a laboratory whose cohort has systematically lower tumor purity adjust the framework's fold-change boundaries?
choices: Use more stringent boundaries than 0.75 and 1.25
Keep 0.75 and 1.25, which copy number theory fixes
Use more permissive boundaries than 0.75 and 1.25
Leave the boundaries and raise the normalized MAD threshold above 0.25
answer: Use more permissive boundaries than 0.75 and 1.25
label: Discussion · recalibration
